These are roughly $7.50 with free shipping, as a set, with shift cables. That's not bad value, frankly. This wal-mart price, here, for a similar, non-brand Shimano part, is ~$25, depending on how you do it, sometimes with tax on top depending where you're buying. Admittedly shipping is likely faster, but is it really worth paying more than 3x the price for that? https://www.walmart.com/ip/Shimano-ST-EF65-3-x-8-Speed-Shift-Brake-Lever-Set/51752066 . I use Wal-Mart as a decent "retail value new," price- most bike shops are around those prices for their parts.

Ironically, 21 speed/7 speed linear pull E51 knockoff sets were more expensive at roughly $10/set. Check out how they blurred out the 'shimano' in the bottom photo. Kinda funny, really, but it tells you what they were going for in terms of cloning. http://www.ebay.com/itm/Black-3x7S-Aluminum-Mountain-speed-Disc-v-Brake-Lever-Shifter-Combo-Set-/182219016879?var=&hash=item2a6d198aaf:m:mg08vMyC2qRra9RloC78oDA . I had a spare rear wheel with an 8 on it already, so it was convenient for me. It doesn't feel any different than the real deal, and the brake handle is made of metal as opposed to plastic (which was my main worry when I hit the 'buy' button.)

Likely the cables it came with are galvanized steel shift cables which rust a bit faster than ordinary stainless steel cables that you'd get from a bike shop. Mine did not come with brake cables- I was able to re-use my rear brake on the front brake, which saved me (about $0.75.).

I also re-utilized the cable housings. While this did not come with linear-pull "noodles" or "Elbows," I did get those with my cheap alloy set. that I paid $4.30 on and those came with brake pads, too, albeit cheap ones that I replaced within a month because they wore down so fast. (That's one part I generally don't skimp on). Still, the levers, cable, and calipers are all working rather well, especially given how inexpensive the whole upgrade was. These calipers are working fairly well. One of them pulls way harder than the other, and adjusting them is proving to be a somewhat minor pain, but I'm sure it'll work out.

So, in terms of an upgrade, it ran me $12.55 for a total upgrade from worn out cantilever/trigger shifter STIs to STI V-Brakes with new brake pads. It took me about 4 weeks for everything to ship- with the calipers taking the longest by over a week. So if you're doing your upgrade, don't start dismantling your commuter when the first part gets in, it may be few days until everything's there.
